evidence_quote: As ‘FRIENDS for Life’ is intended as a primary-aged school based intervention, the trial was comprised of a single cohort of year 5 pupils. Eligibility criteria for participation required schools to be state-funded primary schools (e.g. community, foundation or academy) who have not previously implemented FRIENDS.
resolved_title: FRIENDS for life: Evaluation report and executive summary (EEF, December 2018; Wigelsworth, Squires, Birchinall, Kalambouka, Lendrum, Black, Troncoso, Santos, Ashworth and Britteon)
notes: Recoded from the correct document: text/992-wigelsworth-2018.txt is now the EEF FRIENDS for life report, whose authors match Kraft's citation exactly (earlier recode had the Good Behaviour Game report). Cluster RCT of 122 Year 5 classes (US grade 4) in 79 Kent primary schools; whole classes were randomised and all pupils in them were in the sample with parental opt-out consent only (71 opt-outs, p. 13); the programme was delivered exclusively as a universal intervention (p. 8). School rules (state-funded, not previously implementing FRIENDS, 85 percent baseline data returned) are not selection on need, per tie-breaker 6. Kraft's n of 1,534 equals the usual-provision arm analysed for KS2 (1,476 in the FRIENDS arm, 3,010 total, p. 23), so Kraft appears to have recorded one arm's count rather than the total; effects -0.01 and 0.00 are close to the report's separate maths and reading KS2 results (p. 26), so the effects come from the full sample and mixed_samples is 0. FSM and at-risk subgroup results exist but were not the ones Kraft used. No abstract file and no wwc-codes row.

evidence_quote: an eight-month quantitative posttest experimental study with random assignment of 364 second through sixth grade students to classrooms and random assignment of participating classrooms to control and experimental groups was implemented in a school district located in East Texas
resolved_title: The Effects of "Brain Gym" as a General Education Intervention: Improving Academic Performance and Behaviors (Nussbaum, 2010, dissertation; ERIC ED517276)
notes: Abstract only; no text file and no wwc-codes row. Intervention is described as a tier-one RtI and class-wide general education intervention, so tier-one and at-risk language is program framing, not a sample rule (tie-breaker 7). Abstract reports reading and math t-tests for an at-risk subsample (df 66 and 71) and behavior results for the general classroom; Kraft n=364 matches the full randomized sample, and the at-risk t values imply d near 0.5, not 0.19 and 0.13, so mixed_samples set to 0. Sample includes grades 2 to 6; Kraft assigns grade 4. Verify against full dissertation if it becomes available.
